title: Folded Carapace and Biramous Antennae Water Flea
description: One wholly newly authored enlarged opaque water-flea teaching exterior. A laterally compressed rounded carapace with tapered posterior spine encloses the trunk, while a small exposed rounded head carries one dark compound-eye form, a short downturned rostral contour, two short antennules and two large biramous swimming antennae. Each large antenna has a whole basal shaft, two distinct rami and simplified long terminal setae; five pairs of short leaf-like trunk appendages sit beneath the ventral margin. All carapace sections, head, spine, appendage paths and poses are new, not a shortened water bear, tapered rotifer, recoloured insect or changed limb-count variant. One complete prop, zero scenes, four opaque solid PBR roles. The approximately sixteen-centimetre lateral-display sculpture is greatly enlarged, not life size; its flattened near-side resting datum, solid closed carapace, thickened fine appendages and static spread pose are display conventions. This is not a measured Daphnia species, transparency, complete internal anatomy, brood chamber, eggs, filtering apparatus, individual eye facets, exact seta count, locomotion, live feeding, ecology or diagnostic model. No rig, animation or physical-stability simulation made or verified.
